title: CFC-12 and SF6 ages show that oxygen changes on sigma0 26.5 follow ventilation-age changes in the North Atlantic and North Pacific (GLODAP repeat lines 1985-2021, inverse-Gaussian TTD)
abstract: Question: on the sigma0 = 26.5 density surface, are decadal oxygen and apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) changes, reported at BATS and CalCOFI, caused by water-age (ventilation) changes or by higher respiration rates? Approach: we used CFC-12 and SF6 from 30 occupations of 9 repeat lines in GLODAPv2.2023 (A22, A20, A16N, A05, P02, P03, P01, P16N, P18). We calculated inverse-Gaussian transit-time-distribution mean ages, with the width fitted so that SF6 and CFC-12 agree in the latest occupation. We paired along-track bins between occupations and compared the AOU change with a ventilation-only prediction, OUR x age change. Results: in 16 non-overlapping consecutive pairs on 7 lines, AOU and age changed with the same sign in 13 (sign test p = 0.011; 12-14 of 16 in 8 configurations). Near BATS (A22, 28-36 N) oxygen fell, rose and fell again in 1997-2003, 2003-2012 and 2012-2021, as in the BATS record, while age rose, fell and rose. On the longest pairs, the ventilation-only prediction was 1.19 (1.02-1.44) times the AOU gain on A22, 1.14 on A20, 1.75 on P02 and 1.37 on P16N. Off southern California (P02, 117-130 W) oxygen fell by 33 umol/kg from 1994 to 2013 and age rose by 10-15 yr. Pooled, the AOU change was 0.55 (0.18-0.91) times the prediction with OUR = AOU/age and 1.01 (0.59-1.95) times with OUR from the AOU-age slope. Thus age increases are large enough to explain the AOU gains, and higher respiration rates are not necessary. Limitations: the ventilation fraction is uncertain by about a factor of two because OUR is uncertain; a 1% CFC-12 calibration offset changes the pooled slope to 0.28 or 0.70; we show that a wrong TTD shape alone can make false CFC-12 age trends of -17 to +9 yr in 1994-2013; the TTD width is fitted only in late occupations; P01 and P18 fail the tracer checks; the CalCOFI-end timing is not resolved; we did not do the planned CMIP6 comparison because the model data could not be retrieved in practical time.

display.caption: (a) Repeat lines with CFC-12 on sigma0 26.5 used in this study (blue Atlantic, orange Pacific), with BATS and the CalCOFI grid. (b) Observed AOU change against the ventilation-only prediction (OUR x mean-age change) for consecutive occupations on sigma0 26.5. Filled markers: OUR = AOU/age of the early occupation; open markers: OUR from the AOU-age slope along the line. Bars are 95% bin-bootstrap intervals. Faded: P01, excluded because no inverse-Gaussian width fits its SF6 and CFC-12 data. Dashed: 1:1.

Oxygen and TTD mean age on sigma0 26.5 near BATS (A22, 28-36 N, panels a and c) and off southern California (P02, 117-130 W, panels b and d). Points are means of the bins common to all occupations (bars: standard error over bins). Lines in a and b are the BATS bottle annual means and the CalCOFI core-grid annual anomaly from two prior campaign publications. In b, both series are changes from 1994.

(a) Apparent CFC-12 mean age (inverted with width ratio r = 1) for a steady circulation with a true mean age of 30 yr, when the true TTD is narrower (r = 0.5), wider (r = 1.5) or contains 20% tracer-free water. (b) TTD width ratio at which SF6 and CFC-12 ages agree on sigma0 26.5, for each occupation with at least 8 SF6/CFC-12 pairs.
